research_question: How does the presence of heat and an acid catalyst influence the product of an esterification reaction?
introduction_excerpt: The formation of esters is an important chemical transformation. An esterification reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol produces an ester and water.

reactions.name: Reaction 1 (esterification)
reactions.equation: Acetic acid + pentanol -> pentyl acetate + water
reactions.observation: Fruity odor observed (qualitative evidence of ester formation).

reactions.name: Reaction 2 (acetylation / aspirin synthesis)
reactions.equation: Salicylic acid + acetic anhydride -> acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) + acetic acid
reactions.observation: White solid formed; yields above 100% suggest impurities and incomplete drying.

conclusion.summary: The ester was formed successfully (fruity odor observed). The synthesis of aspirin produced a white solid, but some yields exceeding 100% indicate impurities and incomplete drying.
conclusion.interpretation: Heat and an acid catalyst promote product formation, but measurement and drying steps can bias yield calculations.
